aboutH2: Last Door Recovery Centre: Addiction Treatment for Young Men and Adult Men in New Westminster, BC
intro: Last Door provides addiction recovery services for youth and adult males aged 14 and older. The facility offers private medical detox services, residential recovery programs, and family focus enhancement programs for partners, parents, grandparents, and siblings. Their programs address mental health and substance abuse issues and aim to lift the burden of addiction from their clients’ lives. The average stay at the facility is between 3-5 months.

This listing covers Last Door's home base in New Westminster, where the society runs an adult program for men 19 and over and a youth program for boys aged 14 to 18. Last Door also runs recovery communities in Calgary and Red Deer, Alberta, and owns Keystone, a rural retreat property in Mission about an hour east of Metro Vancouver that clients visit for outdoor therapy, gardening and family retreats.

pillars.title: Recovery Environment and Therapeutic Approaches
pillars.body: Last Door operates in an urban area and provides a home-like setting for their clients. Aside from the programs mentioned above, Last Door also incorporates practical life skills and supervised daily activity in their programs to help clients connect with their sense of responsibility. Clients are encouraged to develop peer support and camaraderie through group work, directed interventions, peer support, and written exercises. Therapeutic groups explore themes of loss, self-esteem, communication, stress, sleep enhancement, anger, leisure and recreation, relationships, and anxiety management. Family work and discharge planning are also integral components of the program.

pillars.title: Last Door’s Long Term Transitional Living Program
pillars.body: Many residents of Last Door also avail of the facility’s long term transitional living program which spans up to a year. This program offers a unique and comprehensive wrap-around service that includes access to room and board, employment assistance, education support, positive peer support, and case management. The client’s medical and clinical progress is continuously monitored and supported through weekly visits from professionals. The goal of the program is to provide long-term support so that clients can maintain recovery and develop an independent and fulfilling life outside of the facility.

pillars.title: Building Recovery Capital
pillars.body: Last Door Recovery Society is considered the Recovery Capital of Canada, and they attribute it to their use of Recovery Capital software, a health-care movement that views clients as a whole. The software measures and monitors clients during post-treatment to assess and build their recovery capital. Clients use their own tablet each week to review their Recovery Capital Assessment and weekly recovery goals, which help Last Door identify areas for improvement.

overview: Last Door Recovery Society is a leading rehab centre located in Metro Vancouver that specializes in delivering comprehensive addiction recovery services. Catering to individuals and families who are struggling with drug and alcohol addiction, Last Door is a fully licensed and accredited facility that has been providing these services for over 35 years. The team of highly qualified and experienced professionals at Last Door is committed to offering a compassionate and supportive environment that is founded on principles such as trust, faith, diversity, and integrity, among others.

location.heading: Last Door Recovery Centre in New Westminster, British Columbia
location.intro: Last Door's primary care houses sit on 8th Street in uptown New Westminster, the small Metro Vancouver city on the Fraser River between Burnaby, Coquitlam and Surrey. Downtown Vancouver is about 30 minutes away by car or SkyTrain, Burnaby and Surrey are 15 to 20 minutes, Abbotsford in the Fraser Valley is under an hour, Victoria is about 3.5 hours with the Tsawwassen ferry, and clients flying in to Vancouver International Airport are met by a driver.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What are the age groups that Last Door offers addiction recovery services to?
faqs.a: It offers addiction recovery services for youth and adult males ages 14 and older: a youth program for ages 14 to 18 and an adult program for men 19 and over.

faqs.q: How much does Last Door cost?
faqs.a: Last Door publishes per-day fees: $325 a day for the Youth Program, $350 a day for the Adult Program and $500 a day for private medical detox or the 10-day Intro to Recovery. A 45-day workplace program starts at $15,750. Fees include food, room and board, counselling and the Family Program, and they are invoiced monthly in advance.

faqs.q: What services are available in Last Door?
faqs.a: Last Door provides private medical detox, residential recovery programs, family focus enhancement programs, long-term transitional living programs.

faqs.q: What is the average stay in the facility?
faqs.a: The average stay at the facility is between 3 to 5 months.

Yes. Last Door runs a private, fee-for-service medical detox for youth and adult males in New Westminster, usually about 5 days, with a physician, a nurse and a recovery coach. A phone screening comes first, and most people move straight into the Intro to Recovery or primary treatment program afterwards.

faqs.q: Is Last Door private? Who pays for treatment?
faqs.a: Last Door is a non-profit registered charity that charges fees for treatment. The centre says fees can be paid by an employer, a First Nations community, private insurance, a workplace benefits provider, family or the client, and Fraser Health may fund people who qualify. Ask about your funding stream on the first call.

faqs.q: Where is Last Door and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 327 8th Street in uptown New Westminster, in Metro Vancouver's Lower Mainland. It is about 30 minutes from downtown Vancouver by car or SkyTrain and 15 to 20 minutes from Burnaby and Surrey. Clients coming from elsewhere in BC or across Canada fly into Vancouver International Airport, where a driver picks them up.

faqs.q: How quickly can I get in?
faqs.a: For people who qualify and have funding in place, Last Door can often admit within 24 hours. It starts with a free phone consultation, and the intake line is answered 7 days a week from 7am to 7pm. Health care workers can send a referral package to intake@lastdoor.org.

faqs.q: What is the long term transitional living program of Last Door?
faqs.a: The long term transitional living program is up to one year, and it offers room and board, employment assistance, education support, positive peer support, and case management.

Continuing care is included in treatment fees. Graduates get lifetime access to the alumni groups that meet on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, free online alumni groups and drop-in time with counsellors, and parents can keep attending the weekly Parents Group. Many residents also move into the transitional living program for up to a year.

faqs.q: How does Last Door measure and monitor clients’ post-treatment?
faqs.a: Last Door uses Recovery Capital software to measure and monitor clients during post-treatment.

Not at the New Westminster site. Its residential youth and adult programs are for males, while the Family Program and transitional living serve all genders and ages. Last Door's Red Deer, Alberta facility is co-ed for men and women.
